Selected work

Things I've built and shipped, plus what's on the bench right now.

Solo developer · 2024 – present

MetaVault

An all-in-one companion for Magic: The Gathering. Scan cards with your phone camera, track what your collection is worth, build decks, and run Commander games with friends. I designed, built, and shipped all of it: web, iOS, backend, and the App Store review process.

Live on the App StoreLive on the web
meta-vault.appApp Store

  • On-device card scanning

    Apple Vision OCR feeds a Scryfall fuzzy-matching pipeline with confidence scoring, so a card lands in your collection seconds after you point the camera at it.

  • Apple Wallet passes

    Generated in Deno Edge Functions, served over Apple's PassKit web service protocol, and refreshed nightly with APNs pushes signed as ES256 JWTs through WebCrypto.

  • Live multiplayer life tracker

    Real-time game-state sync for Commander pods, with turn tracking, life graphs, and game history.

  • Collection-first deck builder

    Pick a commander and it assembles the 99 from cards you already own, then fills the gaps from what the format actually plays. A rules engine on EDHREC and Commander Spellbook data, covered by 72 engine tests.

  • Backend and security

    Supabase Postgres with row-level security, pg_cron jobs for nightly value snapshots, custom auth email with SPF and DKIM, and Sign in with Apple with token revocation on account deletion.

  • Shipping

    React and Vite on AWS Amplify for the web; React Native and Expo through EAS, TestFlight, and App Store review for iOS. 700+ automated tests in CI.

  • Through App Store review

    Worked through two App Store rejections, a permission-prompt wording rule and a login freeze on a new iOS release, then shipped.

  • Secret Lair browser

    All 716 Secret Lair drops matched to their cards by joining Scryfall with MTGJSON data.

  • TCGplayer affiliate

    Card prices link out to TCGplayer through an approved affiliate integration.

Personal project · 2026

Elden Ring, crossed over

A Rust mod framework that puts characters and whole game modes from other games inside Elden Ring, built with AI coding agents and posted as a TikTok series. Five of the clips have passed a million views.

It started with Overwatch's Doomfist in first person: his HUD, cooldowns, and abilities running in my own code instead of Elden Ring's systems. It turned into a roster, including Dragon Ball FighterZ combat, Cyberpunk's Sandevistan, and a Halo Banshee. The rule for every one of them: it has to play like the original.

Watch on TikTok
  • 19M+views across 20 TikTok posts
  • 6.7Mviews on the top clip
  • 2.4Mlikes on the account

  • Reverse-engineered game formats

    Wrote readers for each game's own files to pull out models, animations, sounds, and HUD art: Fallout 4's archives and Havok animations, a Halo animation decoder, and Unity games through AssetRipper.

  • Our own systems, not the host's

    Abilities, hit detection, physics, cameras, and HUDs run in my own Rust code, tuned to each source game's frame data and timings. Elden Ring only supplies the world, enemies, and collision.

  • Shown on TikTok so far

    Overwatch, Halo, Dragon Ball FighterZ, Cyberpunk 2077, Resident Evil 2, Zelda: Ocarina of Time in VR, and a Tesla Roadster.

About

I like owning a product end to end, and I care how it feels, not just whether it runs.

I'm a full-stack engineer who likes designing the data model, building the API, and shaping the front end that sits on top. By day I keep payments, ticketing, and data pipelines running at San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance. After hours it's MetaVault, my master's at Johns Hopkins, and whichever game I'm currently fitting inside Elden Ring.

Lately I spend a lot of time building with LLMs, from the Claude API in production tools to AI coding agents on my mods, and I'm doing my M.S. to go deeper into AI and ML systems.
